model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: A reusable mixin that lets any subject carry declared, context-scoped equivalence and near-equivalence assertions to identifiers held in other systems, preserving exactly the semantics the originating authority asserted and no stronger, together with the authority, justification and confidence behind each assertion.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 governs the declaration, description and declared-semantics validation of alias edges between a host subject identifier and one or more external identifiers. It defines, per relation kind, which formal properties are actually asserted by the owning specification (symmetry, asymmetry, reflexivity, irreflexivity, inverse pairing, composition/transitivity, domain/range applicability, functionality and cardinality force) and which contextual conditions bound the assertion (adopting Dimension, jurisdiction, purpose, subject and object source versions, effective interval). It carries warrant (justification type, confidence with declared semantics, asserting agent reference, review state), explicit non-equivalence constraints, and rules for controlled weakening or strengthening by supersession. It validates and reports declared semantics — contradictions, invalid combinations, cardinality and applicability breaches, and contagion exposure from strong identity assertions. It never computes entailment or closure, never resolves entities, never handles identifier resolution or redirects, and never merges master data.
in_scope: Declaration of alias edges between a host subject identifier and external identifiers, each bound to exactly one governed relation predicate drawn from a catalogue.

Per-kind declaration of formal relation properties: symmetry, asymmetry, reflexivity, irreflexivity, inverse pairing, composition and transitivity, domain/range applicability, functionality and cardinality force.

A declared strength ordering across OWL identity axioms, SKOS mapping properties, identifier succession and relocation relations, schema.org sameAs and probabilistic linkage results, with prohibition on silent promotion or demotion.

Contextual and temporal scoping of an assertion by adopting Dimension, jurisdiction, purpose, subject and object source version, and effective interval, with event time distinguished from observation time.
Context incompatibility rules and authorised, evidenced weakening or strengthening of an existing edge through supersession rather than mutation.
Warrant fields: justification type, confidence value with declared meaning and estimation method, asserting agent reference and review state.
Explicit non-equivalence constraints, declared invalid relation combinations and negated predicates.
Validation and reporting of declared semantics, including contradiction detection and contagion-exposure indicators for strong identity assertions.
Alignment bindings that project declared kinds onto external vocabularies without claiming conformance to them.
out_of_scope: Entity resolution, blocking, similarity computation and match thresholding; only the resulting declared link and its warrant are carried.
Reasoning, entailment materialisation, transitive closure computation and path discovery over an alias graph.
Master-data merge, survivorship rules and golden-record construction.
Identifier minting, allocation, namespace governance and identifier lifecycle for the subject or object themselves.
Identifier resolution and HTTP redirect handling, including following or rewriting relocations.
Enforcement of constraints, remediation of contradictions, or blocking of downstream operations.
Storage, retention execution and audit-trail ownership for records produced under this model.
Access-control decision and enforcement points; this model states access expectations only.
Storage format and interface concerns: JSON, YAML, RDF serialisations, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections, not semantics.
The host subject's own attribute model, classification and lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-XCT-011, the parent cross-cutting identifier and identity model
boundary_notes.distinction: The parent owns subject identity, identifier minting, namespace governance and resolution. WM-XCT-036 owns only the declared properties of assertions made between identifiers, and never mints or resolves an identifier itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Entity resolution and probabilistic record-linkage model
boundary_notes.distinction: The linkage model decides whether two records refer to the same entity, estimating match weights and thresholds. WM-XCT-036 records only what relation was asserted, by whom, with what justification and confidence semantics, and never re-derives or recomputes the decision.

boundary_notes.neighbor: OWL 2 / RDF entailment and closure service
boundary_notes.distinction: Entailment, substitution of identicals and transitive closure are computed by an external reasoner. WM-XCT-036 declares which entailments each kind licenses and validates declared assertions against declared constraints; it does not execute reasoning or materialise inferred edges.

Agents, activities, derivations and generation times are referenced through PROV-aligned pointers. WM-XCT-036 carries the reference and the assertion-specific warrant parameters, not the provenance model's lifecycle or its own provenance graph semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Constraint validation engine and audit-record model
boundary_notes.distinction: Report structure and severity vocabulary are referenced from a SHACL-aligned validation model. Execution of validation, enforcement of outcomes, persistence of reports and audit-trail semantics remain with the referenced engine and the adopting Dimension's audit model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Concept scheme and controlled vocabulary model
boundary_notes.distinction: SKOS mapping properties relate concepts that belong to different concept schemes; scheme membership, labels, notation and intra-scheme hierarchy belong to the vocabulary model. WM-XCT-036 carries the cross-scheme mapping edge and its declared properties only.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Defines SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals, property characteristic axioms, domain/range, inverse properties, property chains and HasKey as the formal vocabulary for declaring relation properties.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Direct Semantics (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Gives the model-theoretic satisfaction conditions for equality, difference, transitivity, symmetry, functionality and property chains, and grounds the substitution consequence of asserted identity.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Quick Reference Guide (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Compact normative listing of axiom names used to name declared property values in the relation-kind catalogue, including owl:deprecated and disjoint property axioms.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language New Features and Rationale (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Explains that HasKey applies only to explicitly named individuals and differs in force from InverseFunctionalProperty, and describes property chains, self restrictions and qualified cardinality.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Normative statements S38-S46 fix the mapping property hierarchy, the inverse pairing of broadMatch/narrowMatch, the symmetry of relatedMatch/closeMatch/exactMatch, the transitivity of exactMatch only, and the disjointness of exactMatch with broadMatch and relatedMatch.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Primer
sources.relevance: Explains why closeMatch is deliberately not transitive so similarity does not propagate across schemes, and why SKOS avoids owl:sameAs between concepts.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Semantics
sources.relevance: Establishes that distinct IRIs may denote the same thing (no unique name assumption) and that entailment regimes are monotonic under an open-world assumption, which is why alias edges must be asserted rather than inferred from difference of identifier.

sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Syntax
sources.relevance: Triple terms and reifiers allow a mapping statement to be annotated with certainty, source and time without asserting it, and RDF datasets/named graphs provide the context-scoping projection.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the referenced agent, activity, attribution, derivation and generation-time vocabulary for assertion warrant, and prov:alternateOf/specializationOf as weaker-than-identity alternatives.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Separates validation from inference, and defines the validation report structure (conforms, focus node, source constraint component, severity) referenced for declared-semantics reporting.

sources.title: schema.org property: sameAs
sources.relevance: Defines sameAs as the URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity, with domain Thing and expected type URL, and no declared algebraic properties or entailment.

sources.title: schema.org Releases
sources.relevance: Fixes the vocabulary version against which the schema.org alignment is recorded, so alignment tables can be versioned rather than assumed stable.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: Defines replaces / isReplacedBy as an inverse documentary pair for succession and supersession, plus isVersionOf, conformsTo, valid and modified used for source versioning and validity intervals.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Defines 301/308 permanent and 302/303/307 temporary redirection, establishing that permanent relocation of a resource permits reference rewriting but is not an assertion of identity between described things.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Fixes the timestamp grammar requiring seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and the -00:00 convention for an unknown local offset, used for effective intervals and assertion times.

sources.title: SSSOM Specification: Mapping data model and metadata elements
sources.relevance: Provides the operational metadata vocabulary for a mapping: subject/predicate/object, mapping_justification, confidence, mapping_cardinality enumeration, predicate_modifier 'Not', source versions, author, date, tool and licence.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM)
sources.organization: Database: The Journal of Biological Databases and Curation (Oxford University Press)
sources.relevance: Documents why mapping predicates must not be treated uniformly, why imprecision and incompleteness must be made explicit, and how blind mapping walks conflate distinct concepts.

sources.title: When owl:sameAs Isn't the Same: An Analysis of Identity in Linked Data
sources.organization: International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC 2010), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 6496, Springer
sources.relevance: Argues that owl:sameAs encodes one point on a similarity scale and is often too strong for its uses, and identifies referentially opaque contexts where identity substitution must not be applied — the counterexample basis for contextual equivalence.

sources.title: Revisiting the probabilistic method of record linkage
sources.organization: arXiv (stat.ME), Dasylva, Goussanou, Ajavon and Abousaleh
sources.relevance: Shows that probabilistic linkage produces error-bounded statistical links dependent on model assumptions and clerical review, not logical identity — grounding the rule that a linkage score never licenses an identity axiom.

bundles.name: Declared formal relation semantics
bundles.description: What each alias relation kind actually asserts: its owning specification, its semantic class, its declared algebraic properties, its applicability and its cardinality force. Covers the catalogue of kinds, the strength ordering between them, symmetry and inversion, composition and transitivity, and domain/range and cardinality declarations.
bundles.rationale: Alias edges are routinely treated as one uniform symmetric-transitive relation. The cited specifications contradict that: owl:sameAs licenses substitution of identicals, skos:exactMatch is transitive while skos:closeMatch is deliberately not, broadMatch and narrowMatch form an inverse pair, dcterms:isReplacedBy is directional succession, HTTP permanent redirect is relocation of a resource, and schema.org sameAs declares no algebra at all. A defensible model must declare properties per kind rather than assume them.

layers.name: Relation-kind catalogue and semantic strength
layers.description: Governed catalogue of the relation predicates an alias edge may name, each with the semantics its owning specification actually licenses, and the partial order of strength that governs how an incoming assertion may be re-expressed locally.

findings.name: Relation-kind semantic profile
findings.description: Every alias edge names exactly one governed predicate, and each predicate carries a normative profile taken from its owning specification. The profile records the semantic class actually asserted: referential identity of individuals (owl:sameAs, licensing substitution), class co-extension (owl:equivalentClass, not individual identity), graded cross-scheme equivalence (skos:exactMatch, skos:closeMatch), cross-scheme hierarchy (skos:broadMatch, skos:narrowMatch), cross-scheme association (skos:relatedMatch), documentary succession (dcterms:replaces, dcterms:isReplacedBy), resolution-level relocation (HTTP 301/308), reference-page identity indication with no declared entailment (schema.org sameAs), and statistical linkage results carrying a score rather than an axiom. The profile also records which entailments are licensed and which are commonly assumed but not licensed.

questions.text: Which single governed relation predicate does this alias edge assert, and which specification and version owns its meaning?
Does the asserted predicate claim referential identity, class co-extension, graded equivalence, cross-scheme hierarchy, documentary succession, resolution-level relocation, or a statistical link?
answer_data: Citation of the clause that fixes the class
Whether substitution of identicals is licensed

questions.text: Which body governs this predicate's normative semantics and may change them without the adopting Dimension's consent?
answer_data: Local review obligation on external version change

questions.text: Which entailments does the owning specification actually license for this predicate, and which are widely assumed but unlicensed?
answer_data: Explicitly unlicensed or disclaimed entailment list
Known misuse notes with source citation

data_elements.name: Predicate IRI
data_elements.description: Resolvable IRI of the relation predicate as minted by its owning specification, or by the adopting Dimension for a local kind.

data_elements.name: Semantic class code
data_elements.description: Coded semantic class of the predicate: identity, co-extension, graded-equivalence, hierarchical, associative, succession, relocation, reference-indication or statistical-link.

data_elements.name: Owning specification reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the specification document and clause that fixes the predicate's semantics, with the version or publication date in force.

data_elements.name: Licensed entailment set
data_elements.description: Enumerated entailments the owning specification licenses for the predicate, each with its clause citation.

data_elements.name: Disclaimed entailment note
data_elements.description: Entailments commonly assumed for this predicate that the owning specification does not license, recorded to prevent silent over-reading.

artifacts.name: Relation-kind semantic profile record
artifacts.description: A durable record of one relation kind: its predicate IRI, semantic class, owning specification and version, declared algebraic properties, applicability, cardinality force, licensed and disclaimed entailments, and deprecation state. It is descriptive of an external specification and confers no conformance claim.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the predicate IRI minted by the owning standards body where one exists; for a Dimension-local kind, by a resolvable IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace; failing both, by a ULID marked as locally minted. Version or publication date of the owning specification is a qualifier, never the identifier.

findings.name: Strength ordering and preservation on carriage
findings.description: The catalogue is partially ordered by asserted strength, and carriage of an external assertion must preserve the strongest semantics actually asserted and no stronger. Concretely: a schema.org sameAs value or a probabilistic linkage result must not be re-encoded as owl:sameAs; skos:closeMatch must not be promoted to skos:exactMatch; an HTTP 308 relocation or a dcterms:isReplacedBy succession must not be read as identity of the described thing; and a high confidence value never licenses promotion. Some pairs are incomparable rather than ordered (for example associative relatedness versus documentary succession), and unrepresentable incoming kinds are recorded as lossy with a justification instead of being approximated upward.

questions.text: What is the strongest relation kind the originating authority actually asserted for this edge, as opposed to what a consumer inferred?
Is re-encoding the incoming kind into a different local kind permitted here, and what justification must be recorded?
Which promotions between kinds are prohibited outright regardless of any confidence value?
What must be recorded when an incoming assertion cannot be expressed in the local catalogue without loss of meaning?

data_elements.name: Source-asserted kind
data_elements.description: The predicate IRI exactly as asserted by the originating system, retained verbatim even when a different local kind is used.

data_elements.name: Strength relation code
data_elements.description: Relation of the local kind to the source kind in the declared partial order: equal, weaker, stronger or incomparable. A value of stronger is invalid for carriage.

data_elements.name: Lossy encoding flag
data_elements.description: Indicates that the local catalogue cannot express the incoming semantics exactly, requiring a recorded description of the loss.

data_elements.name: Re-encoding justification
data_elements.description: Free-text justification and deciding role for any change of predicate between the source assertion and the stored assertion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The strength ordering is declared reference data over kinds that are already carried by the relation-kind semantic profile record, and the per-edge preservation outcome is a small set of typed fields on the alias assertion itself. Minting a separate ordering document would duplicate the profile records, create a second place where an external specification version change must be reflected, and invite drift between the ordering and the profiles it orders. Recording the ordering inline on the profiles and the outcome inline on the assertion keeps a single authoritative statement per kind.

layers.name: Declared algebraic and structural properties
layers.description: Per-kind declarations of symmetry and inversion, composition and transitivity, reflexivity, and applicability and cardinality force — each stated only where the owning specification actually asserts it, with the axiomatic force of the assertion recorded.

findings.name: Symmetry, inversion and reflexivity declarations
findings.description: Each kind declares, separately and with axiomatic force noted, whether it is symmetric, asymmetric or neither; whether it has a declared inverse predicate and whether the inverse edge may be materialised; and whether a self-edge is permitted, required or prohibited. SKOS declares relatedMatch, closeMatch and exactMatch symmetric and narrowMatch the inverse of broadMatch; owl:sameAs is symmetric and reflexive as equality; dcterms:replaces and isReplacedBy are a documentary inverse pair without an OWL axiom; HTTP relocation is directional; schema.org sameAs declares no inverse. Where the source records only one direction, the reverse must not be reported as asserted unless symmetry is declared for that kind.

questions.text: Is this kind declared symmetric, asymmetric, or neither by its owning specification, and with what axiomatic force?
answer_data: Axiomatic force code covering formal axiom, documentary statement or undeclared

questions.text: Does this kind have a declared inverse predicate, and must the inverse edge be materialised or left implicit?
answer_data: Whether the inverse pairing is an OWL axiom or a documentary convention

questions.text: Is a self-edge, where subject and object identifiers are the same, permitted, required or prohibited for this kind?
answer_data: Handling rule for a submitted self-edge

questions.text: When the originating record captures only one direction, may the reverse direction be reported as asserted rather than derived?
answer_data: Required annotation when a direction is derived rather than asserted

data_elements.name: Symmetry declaration
data_elements.description: Coded declaration of symmetric, asymmetric or undeclared for the kind, with the axiomatic force of the declaration.

data_elements.name: Inverse predicate reference
data_elements.description: IRI of the declared inverse predicate where one exists, together with whether the pairing is an OWL inverse axiom or a documentary convention.

data_elements.name: Reflexivity declaration
data_elements.description: Coded declaration of reflexive, irreflexive or undeclared for the kind, governing whether self-edges are accepted.

data_elements.name: Direction asserted
data_elements.description: Records whether the stored direction is the one the originating authority asserted, or a direction obtained under a declared symmetry or inverse rule.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Symmetry, inverse pairing and reflexivity are three enumerated declarations attached to the relation-kind semantic profile plus one direction field on each assertion. They have no independent existence, no separate lifecycle and no separate authority from the kind whose semantics they describe. Splitting them into their own artifact would fragment a single normative profile across records that must always be read together, and would create the possibility of a profile whose declared algebra disagrees with itself.

findings.name: Composition, transitivity and path admissibility
findings.description: Whether an edge A to B of kind K1 and an edge B to C of kind K2 yield anything about A to C is decided by a declared composition rule for the ordered kind pair, not assumed. owl:sameAs and skos:exactMatch are declared transitive; skos:closeMatch is deliberately not, so similarity does not propagate across schemes; mixed pairs yield at most the weaker kind, and many yield nothing. OWL property chain axioms are the formal device for stating such compositions. A result may never exceed the weakest link in the supplied sequence, and a formally composable chain is still inadmissible when adjacent edges are context-incompatible. Closure computation and path discovery are performed elsewhere; this model states the rule and evaluates it over a caller-supplied sequence.

questions.text: For this ordered pair of declared kinds, what result kind, if any, does the declared composition rule yield?
answer_data: Result kind IRI or explicit none

questions.text: Which ordered kind pairs are declared non-composable, so that no result may be reported at all?
answer_data: Source clause establishing the absence of transitivity

questions.text: How does the weakest link in a supplied edge sequence bound the strength of any reported result?
answer_data: Bound violation code when a caller requests a stronger result

questions.text: Under what conditions is a formally composable chain still inadmissible because of context, conditionality or a negated edge?
answer_data: Identifier of the offending edge in the sequence

questions.text: Which component discovers paths and computes closure, and what does this model provide in its place?
answer_data: Entailment regime or profile parameter carried locally
Statement of the locally provided rule-evaluation output

data_elements.name: Left kind of the ordered pair
data_elements.description: Predicate IRI of the first edge in the ordered pair the composition rule governs.

data_elements.name: Right kind of the ordered pair
data_elements.description: Predicate IRI of the second edge in the ordered pair the composition rule governs.

data_elements.name: Composed result kind
data_elements.description: Predicate IRI of the strongest kind the rule licenses for the composed pair, absent when the pair is non-composable.

data_elements.name: Composable flag
data_elements.description: Boolean stating whether the ordered pair composes at all under the declared rule set.

data_elements.name: External closure owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external reasoner, entailment regime or closure service responsible for materialising inferences, with the profile or regime parameter carried locally.

artifacts.name: Declared relation composition rule record
artifacts.description: A durable record stating, for one ordered pair of relation kinds, whether composition is licensed, what the strongest licensed result kind is, the bounding weakest-link rule, and the source clause supporting or denying transitivity. It is a declaration consumed by external evaluators; it does not itself compute or store closure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative rule identifier assigned by the owning rule set where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI formed in a Dimension-controlled namespace from the ordered pair of predicate IRIs; failing both, by a ULID marked as locally minted.

findings.name: Applicability, functionality and cardinality force
findings.description: Each kind declares which node kinds may occupy subject and object position, and what force any cardinality statement carries. OWL 2 DL restricts SameIndividual to individuals and equivalentClass to classes, so asserting identity between classes changes the reasoning regime; SKOS mapping properties relate concepts, which is why merging concepts with owl:sameAs conflicts with SKOS label constraints; schema.org sameAs takes a URL value on a Thing; relocation relations hold between resolvable locators, not between the things they describe. Separately, a mapping cardinality value such as one-to-one is descriptive metadata about an observed mapping set, whereas FunctionalProperty, InverseFunctionalProperty and HasKey are axioms — and HasKey applies only to explicitly named individuals. Declaring a mapping one-to-one therefore entails nothing.

questions.text: Which node kinds may occupy the subject and object positions for this relation kind?
Is the recorded cardinality descriptive metadata about an observed mapping set or an enforced axiom, and which specification gives it that force?
answer_data: Axiom reference where the force is axiomatic
Statement of what the value does and does not entail

questions.text: What cardinality is actually observed for this mapping set, and over which subject and object sources and versions was it measured?
Is each endpoint a real-world entity, a concept in a scheme, a document, or a resolvable locator, and does the kind respect that distinction?
answer_data: Referent mismatch violation code where the kind is inapplicable

data_elements.name: Permitted subject node kind
data_elements.description: Coded node kind allowed in subject position for the relation kind, such as individual, class, concept, document or locator.

data_elements.name: Permitted object node kind
data_elements.description: Coded node kind allowed in object position for the relation kind, including the case where only a resolvable URL is permitted.

data_elements.name: Declared mapping cardinality
data_elements.description: Coded cardinality of the mapping such as one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many or a zero-sided value, recorded as descriptive metadata.

data_elements.name: Cardinality force
data_elements.description: Whether the cardinality statement is descriptive, or is backed by a functional, inverse-functional or key axiom, with the axiom reference.

data_elements.name: Endpoint referent type
data_elements.description: Coded referent type for each endpoint distinguishing entity, concept, document and resolvable locator, used to detect inapplicable kinds.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Applicability and cardinality force are typed fields that belong to the relation-kind semantic profile, and observed cardinality is a measured attribute of an assertion set that changes whenever a source version changes. None of them has an independent owner, retention class or audience. Holding them inline keeps the declaration in one place with the specification version it was derived from, and avoids a second record that could contradict the owning specification after an external version change.

bundles.name: Contextual validity, warrant and conflict reporting
bundles.description: The conditions under which a declared equivalence actually holds, the warrant that supports it, and the reporting of contradictions and exposure. Covers context and temporal scoping, context incompatibility and controlled strength change, justification and confidence, and explicit non-equivalence constraints with contagion-exposure indicators.
bundles.rationale: Identity assertions in federated settings are rarely unconditional. The cited literature shows that owl:sameAs is one point on a similarity scale and that referentially opaque contexts exist where substitution must not be applied; mapping standards require justification, confidence and source versions to be explicit precisely because imprecision is the normal case. Because equality licenses substitution, one false strong assertion propagates, so declared non-equivalence and exposure reporting are structural requirements rather than optional metadata.

layers.name: Context, time and controlled strength change
layers.description: How an assertion is bound to a Dimension, jurisdiction, purpose, source versions and effective interval; when two contexts are incompatible; and how strength or scope may be changed only by an authorised, evidenced superseding assertion.

findings.name: Context and temporal binding of an assertion
findings.description: An alias assertion is bound to the context in which it is claimed to hold: the adopting Dimension, an optional jurisdiction or territorial scope, one or more purposes of use, the subject-source and object-source versions in force, and an effective interval expressed with explicit offsets. Assertion time, the interval over which the equivalence is claimed to hold, and the time this model observed or ingested the assertion are recorded separately. An assertion submitted without a declared context is stored as scope-unknown and must never be read as globally valid, which follows from the absence of a unique name assumption and the open-world reading of the underlying data: silence is not a claim of universality.

questions.text: Over which effective interval is this equivalence asserted to hold, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset?
answer_data: Effective to instant or open-ended marker

questions.text: Which jurisdiction or territorial scope conditions this assertion, and is that scope exclusive?
answer_data: Authority that fixed the jurisdictional scope

questions.text: Which Dimension and which purposes does the assertion serve, and who owns the binding?
answer_data: Binding owner role and contact reference

questions.text: Which subject-source and object-source versions were in force when the assertion was made?
How is an assertion interpreted when no context at all is declared?

data_elements.name: Adopting Dimension reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the Dimension within which the assertion is claimed to hold and which owns the context binding.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction or territorial scope code
data_elements.description: Coded jurisdiction conditioning the assertion, supplied by the adopting Dimension; absent where the assertion is not jurisdictionally conditioned.

data_elements.name: Purpose of use code
data_elements.description: Coded purpose or application context for which the equivalence is asserted to be adequate.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: Start and optional end instants over which the equivalence is asserted to hold, each an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Assertion instant
data_elements.description: Event time at which the asserting agent made the claim, distinct from the interval over which the claim holds.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion instant
data_elements.description: Time at which this model observed or ingested the assertion, recorded separately from the assertion instant and always retained when the two differ.

data_elements.name: Scope declared flag
data_elements.description: Boolean indicating whether any context attribute was declared; false marks the assertion scope-unknown rather than global.

artifacts.name: Alias assertion context binding record
artifacts.description: A durable record binding one alias assertion to its Dimension, jurisdiction, purposes, subject and object source versions and effective interval, with assertion time and observation time held separately. It states the conditions of the claim; it does not evaluate whether the conditions currently obtain.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative assertion identifier assigned by the originating mapping system of record; where none exists, by a governed IRI or reifier IRI minted in a Dimension-controlled namespace; failing both, by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The effective interval and source versions are qualifiers and are never used as the identifier.

findings.name: Context incompatibility and controlled strength change
findings.description: Two assertions are context-incompatible when their declared scopes cannot both apply: disjoint jurisdictions, mutually exclusive purposes, non-overlapping effective intervals, or subject and object source versions that are not co-valid. Incompatible edges must not be composed and must not be treated as corroborating one another; a declared scope compared against a scope-unknown assertion is reported as undetermined, never as compatible. Strength or scope may change only through a superseding assertion carrying an authority reference, a reason and a new effective interval — never by silent mutation. Weakening and strengthening carry different evidence bars, since strengthening enlarges what may be substituted while weakening only reduces it.

questions.text: Which declared scope attributes make two assertions incompatible rather than merely different?
answer_data: Undetermined outcome rule for scope-unknown comparisons

questions.text: What state does an assertion enter when its effective interval has ended or its source version has been superseded?
answer_data: Trigger that caused the state change
Whether the assertion remains readable and to whom

questions.text: Who is authorised to weaken or strengthen a declared edge, and what evidence bar applies to strengthening?
answer_data: Evidence bar description per change direction
Authority reference recorded on the change

questions.text: How is a superseding assertion linked to the assertion it replaces without deleting the original?
answer_data: Retention treatment of the superseded record

questions.text: Which chains become inadmissible once one link is context-incompatible with the next?

data_elements.name: Context incompatibility code
data_elements.description: Coded reason two context bindings cannot both apply, such as disjoint jurisdiction, exclusive purpose, non-overlapping interval or non-co-valid source versions.

data_elements.name: Strength change direction
data_elements.description: Coded direction of a superseding change: weakened, strengthened, scope narrowed, scope widened or retracted.

data_elements.name: Change authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the role or body that authorised the strength or scope change, together with the evidence bar applied.

data_elements.name: Superseded assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference from the superseding assertion to the assertion it replaces, mirroring documentary replaces and isReplacedBy semantics.

data_elements.name: Assertion state code
data_elements.description: Coded state of the assertion: active, expired, superseded, retracted or deprecated, with the trigger recorded.

artifacts.name: Strength and scope supersession record
artifacts.description: An append-only record of one authorised change to an existing alias edge: the superseded and superseding assertion references, the change direction, the authority and reason, and the new effective interval. It records that a change was made and on whose authority; it does not enforce the change downstream and is not the audit trail of the change.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative supersession identifier from the mapping system of record where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace combined with a monotonic sequence number for the parent assertion; failing both, by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.

layers.name: Warrant, non-equivalence and declared-semantics reporting
layers.description: The evidential basis reported for each assertion, and the declared negative constraints, invalid combinations and exposure indicators that make a false strong identity assertion detectable before it propagates.

findings.name: Justification, confidence and asserting authority
findings.description: Every edge carries a justification type stating how the mapping was arrived at — human curation, lexical or string similarity, logical derivation, or unspecified — plus the asserting agent and the activity or tool that generated it, with a generation time. Confidence, where present, is a value on a declared scale whose meaning and estimation method must be stated: a probabilistic linkage posterior derived from a statistical model with its own error rates and assumptions is not the same quantity as a curator's subjective degree of belief. Absence of confidence is recorded as unknown and never defaulted to certainty, and no confidence value ever changes the relation kind.

answer_data: Activity or tool reference with version

What does the recorded confidence value mean, on what scale, and by which estimation method was it produced?
How is the absence of any confidence estimate represented so that it cannot be read as certainty?
answer_data: Prohibition on defaulting to a numeric value
Consumer handling rule for unknown confidence
