data_elements.name: Mapping justification code
data_elements.description: Coded justification for the assertion, such as manual curation, lexical match, logical derivation or unspecified.

data_elements.name: Confidence value
data_elements.description: Numeric confidence on a declared scale; absent rather than zero or one when no estimate exists.

data_elements.name: Confidence semantics declaration
data_elements.description: Declaration of what the confidence quantity means, its range, and the estimation method that produced it, including model assumptions where statistical.

data_elements.name: Asserting agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent, and optionally the activity or tool with version, credited with the assertion under the referenced provenance model.

data_elements.name: Review state
data_elements.description: Coded review state of the assertion, such as unreviewed, reviewed, disputed or withdrawn, with the reviewer reference where applicable.

artifacts.name: Assertion warrant record
artifacts.description: A durable record of the evidential basis for one alias assertion: justification type, confidence with its declared semantics and estimation method, asserting agent and activity references, generation time and review state. It references the provenance model rather than restating its lifecycle.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative warrant or curation-record identifier from the originating mapping system where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace; failing both, by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.

findings.name: Non-equivalence constraints, contradiction and contagion exposure
findings.description: Explicit not-same declarations are first-class: difference axioms between individuals, a negated-predicate modifier stating that a mapping does not hold, and standard disjointness such as exact match being disjoint with broad match and with related match. Against these the model reports, without enforcing: direct contradiction where identity is asserted and denied over the same pair in compatible contexts; invalid combinations such as exact match together with related match, or identity together with difference; breaches of declared applicability or cardinality; and contagion exposure — indicators of how many distinct authoritative identifiers, sources or classes a strength-of-identity edge would draw together, because equality licenses substitution and one false strong assertion propagates to everything reachable from it. Reports are derived and non-authoritative; disposition, repair and retention belong elsewhere.

questions.text: Which not-same or disjointness constraints are declared over this pair of identifiers or over this predicate set?
Which declared combinations are reported as invalid, and at what severity?
What exposure indicators are reported for a strength-of-identity assertion before a consumer accepts it?
answer_data: Count of distinct authoritative sources drawn together
Count of distinct declared classes or types drawn together
Presence of any conflicting not-same declaration

questions.text: When a contradiction is reported, who decides the disposition and who carries it out?
answer_data: Executing component reference outside this model

questions.text: How long is a declared-semantics report kept, and which policy owns its retention and audit trail?
answer_data: Audit model reference that holds the trail

data_elements.name: Non-equivalence declaration reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an explicit not-same declaration over a pair of identifiers, or to a negated-predicate modifier stating that a mapping does not hold.

data_elements.name: Violation code
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of a declared-semantics check, such as identity contradicted by difference, disjoint predicates co-asserted, applicability breach or cardinality breach.

data_elements.name: Result severity
data_elements.description: Coded severity of a reported result, aligned to violation, warning and informational levels of the referenced validation model.

data_elements.name: Contagion exposure indicator
data_elements.description: Quantified indicator of how many distinct authoritative sources, identifier schemes or declared classes a strength-of-identity assertion would draw together, with the scope over which it was computed.

data_elements.name: Evaluated assertion-set digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the exact assertion set and constraint version a report evaluated, so a report can be shown stale without re-running validation.

data_elements.name: Disposition owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the role that decides and the component that executes the disposition of a reported conflict, both outside this model's boundary.

artifacts.name: Declared-semantics conformance report
artifacts.description: A derived, non-authoritative report over a named assertion set: overall conformance, individual results with focus pair, violation code, severity and source constraint reference, plus contagion exposure indicators and the digest of the evaluated set. It reports only; it applies no remediation, blocks no operation, and its persistence, retention and audit trail are owned by the referenced validation and audit models.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the report identifier assigned by the executing validation service where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace combined with a monotonic sequence number per evaluated assertion set; failing both, by a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The evaluated-set digest is a qualifier, not the identifier.

functions.name: Declare a relation kind and its formal properties
functions.description: Register a relation predicate in the governed catalogue with the properties its owning specification actually asserts, the axiomatic force of each, and its position in the strength ordering.
inputs: Predicate IRI and owning specification reference with version or publication date
Declared symmetry, reflexivity, inverse pairing, applicability and cardinality force values with clause citations
Proposed strength class relative to existing catalogue entries
outputs: Catalogue change note stating whether the kind is new, revised or deprecates an existing kind
preconditions: The predicate IRI resolves and is not a redefinition of a standard predicate under altered semantics
Every declared property is supported by a cited clause or is explicitly recorded as undeclared
The owning specification version is recorded so later external changes are detectable
effects: The kind becomes available for binding to assertions
Consumers can read licensed and explicitly disclaimed entailments before relying on the kind
No existing assertion is reinterpreted; a semantics change requires a new kind identifier

functions.name: Bind an alias assertion to kind, context and warrant
functions.description: Record one alias edge with exactly one catalogued kind, a context binding or explicit scope-unknown marker, and its warrant, preserving the strength the originating authority asserted.
inputs: Subject identifier and object identifier with their referent types
Catalogued relation kind and the source-asserted predicate retained verbatim
Context binding attributes or an explicit scope-unknown marker
Warrant fields: justification type, optional confidence with declared semantics, asserting agent reference
outputs: Alias assertion record with references to its context binding and warrant record
Lossy-encoding note where the incoming kind is not expressible in the local catalogue
preconditions: The named kind exists in the catalogue and is not deprecated
Subject and object referent types satisfy the kind's declared applicability
The local kind is not stronger than the kind the originating authority asserted
Assertion time and observation time are both supplied
effects: The assertion becomes available for declared-semantics validation and reporting
No entailment is materialised, no inverse edge is created unless symmetry is declared, and no host record is merged

functions.name: Validate declared semantics and report results
functions.description: Check a supplied assertion set against declared applicability, cardinality force, disjointness and non-equivalence constraints, and emit a report with severities and contagion exposure indicators.
inputs: Reference and digest of the assertion set to evaluate
Constraint or shape version and the declared non-equivalence declarations in force
Scope parameters for exposure indicator computation
outputs: Declared-semantics conformance report with overall conformance flag and individual results
Contagion exposure indicators for strength-of-identity assertions
Explicit undetermined outcomes where a comparison involves a scope-unknown assertion
preconditions: Every assertion in the set resolves to a catalogued kind
Each assertion carries a context binding or an explicit scope-unknown marker
The constraint version is recorded so the report can later be shown stale
effects: A report is produced and referenced from the assertion set
No assertion is modified, no remediation is applied, no downstream operation is blocked
Persistence, retention and audit of the report are handed to the referenced validation and audit models

functions.name: Evaluate a composition rule over a supplied edge sequence
functions.description: For an ordered edge sequence supplied by the caller, report the strongest kind the declared composition rules license, or an explicit non-composable or inadmissible outcome with a reason.
inputs: Caller-supplied finite ordered sequence of edges, each naming a catalogued kind and a context key
outputs: Composed result kind bounded by the weakest link, or an explicit none
Non-composable or inadmissible outcome with reason code and the offending edge or adjacent pair
preconditions: The edge sequence is supplied by the caller; this function does not discover it
Each edge names a catalogued kind and either a context binding or a scope-unknown marker
Adjacent edges have been assessed for context compatibility
effects: A reported outcome is returned to the caller
No graph is traversed, no path is discovered, no closure is materialised, and no new assertion is created

functions.name: Assess compatibility of two context bindings
functions.description: Compare two declared context bindings attribute by attribute and report compatible, incompatible with codes, or undetermined.
inputs: Two context binding records or scope-unknown markers
Comparison rules for jurisdiction, purpose, effective interval and source-version co-validity
outputs: Compatibility verdict of compatible, incompatible or undetermined
Incompatibility code set naming each attribute that conflicts
preconditions: Both bindings declare comparable attributes or an explicit unknown for each attribute compared
Interval comparison uses instants with seconds and explicit offsets
effects: The verdict is available to composition evaluation and to validation reporting
A comparison involving a scope-unknown binding is reported as undetermined and never as compatible

functions.name: Record an authorised strength or scope change
functions.description: Create a superseding assertion and its supersession record when an existing edge is weakened, strengthened, rescoped or retracted, retaining the original.
inputs: New relation kind or new scope attributes and new effective interval
Authority reference, change direction and reason
Evidence reference where the change strengthens the edge
outputs: Supersession record linking prior and superseding assertions
Updated state on the prior assertion marking it superseded or retracted
preconditions: The acting role holds the declared authority for the change direction
A strengthening change meets the declared evidence bar
The prior assertion is active or expired, not already retracted
The new effective interval is expressed with seconds and an explicit offset
effects: The prior assertion is retained and readable, never mutated in place
The strength and scope history of the edge remains reconstructible
Downstream propagation and enforcement of the change are left to the consuming systems

composition.target: WM-XCT-011 parent cross-cutting identifier and identity model
composition.purpose: Inherit subject identity scope from the parent and contribute only the declared formal and contextual properties of assertions made between identifiers. Identifier minting, namespace governance, resolution and the identifier's own lifecycle remain with the parent and are not reproduced here.

composition.target: Host entity, concept or record models adopting federated identity equivalence
composition.purpose: Attach declared alias edges, context bindings and warrant to a host subject without altering the host's own identity scheme, attributes or lifecycle. The host remains the system of record for its subject; this mixin adds only equivalence assertions about it.

composition.target: External OWL 2 and RDF entailment, reasoning and closure service
composition.purpose: Carry the service reference and the binding parameters it needs, such as the entailment regime or profile, so that declared kinds can be evaluated externally. Reasoning, substitution of identicals, closure computation and materialisation of inferred edges are executed by the target and are never performed or stored here.

composition.target: Entity resolution and probabilistic record-linkage model
composition.purpose: Carry the candidate-link identifier, justification type, score and estimation-method reference produced by the target. Blocking, comparison-vector construction, weight estimation, threshold selection and clerical review remain with the target and are not re-derived here.

composition.target: Provenance and attribution model aligned to PROV-O
composition.purpose: Reference agents, activities, derivations and generation times as the warrant for an assertion. The provenance model owns its own record lifecycle, graph semantics and bundle handling; only assertion-specific pointers are held locally.

composition.target: Constraint validation and reporting model aligned to SHACL
composition.purpose: Bind shape and severity vocabulary and receive the report structure for declared-semantics results. Execution of validation, enforcement of outcomes, report persistence, retention and audit-trail semantics are owned by the target.

composition.target: Identifier redirect, succession and replacement handling model
composition.purpose: Carry the declared relocation or succession kind and its explicit non-identity semantics so consumers do not over-read a permanent redirect or a replacement statement as entity identity. Resolution, redirect following and reference rewriting are executed by the target.

composition.target: W3C OWL 2 identity vocabulary: owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom, owl:equivalentClass
composition.purpose: Map catalogued kinds and non-equivalence declarations onto OWL 2 axioms, recording the licensed entailments and the applicability restriction to individuals, without claiming conformance to any OWL 2 profile absent published validation evidence.

composition.target: W3C SKOS mapping vocabulary: exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, relatedMatch
composition.purpose: Map catalogued kinds onto SKOS mapping properties, preserving the declared symmetry set, the inverse pairing of broad and narrow match, the transitivity of exact match only, and the disjointness of exact match with broad and related match.

composition.target: schema.org sameAs property, vocabulary release v30.0
composition.purpose: Map the reference-page identity indication onto a catalogued kind with URL-valued objects and no declared algebraic properties, so publication-oriented sameAs values are never promoted to logical identity.

composition.target: SSSOM Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings
composition.purpose: Field-level alignment for justification, confidence, mapping cardinality, subject and object source versions, negated-predicate modifier, author and tool, so mapping sets can be exchanged without reinterpreting predicate semantics.

owner_package_requirements: Name one accountable owner for the relation-kind catalogue and one for the alias assertion set; the two may differ, but neither may be left unassigned while assertions are accepted.

Declare the Dimension's default context — jurisdictions, purposes and source-version conventions — and state explicitly that an assertion without a declared context is scope-unknown rather than globally valid.
Publish the confidence semantics and estimation methods the Dimension accepts before any numeric confidence value is stored, including the range and what the number is a probability or degree of.
Name the external reasoner or validator referenced for evaluation and reporting, and record that no conformance to an external profile is claimed without published validation evidence.
Record the review cadence for external specification version changes, since a change at the owning body can alter what a catalogued kind means.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Governed predicates keep the IRI minted by their owning body and are never re-minted locally. A Dimension-local relation kind uses a resolvable IRI under a namespace the Dimension controls, and must never reuse or shadow a standard predicate IRI with altered semantics. Local identifiers for assertions, context bindings, warrant records and supersession records are lower-kebab-case within the model namespace and carry no date-like component.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-036 for model WM-XCT-036 in the world-model record plane
Parent registry entry WM-XCT-011 for identifier and identity scope
The adopting Dimension's relation-kind catalogue registry, holding one profile record per catalogued predicate
The adopting Dimension's jurisdiction and purpose code lists used by context bindings

canonicalization_rules: The canonical key of an assertion is the tuple of subject identifier, predicate IRI, object identifier and context-binding key; multi-valued fields are ordered lexicographically by IRI or code before hashing.

For a kind declared symmetric, the edge is stored in one canonical direction determined by lexicographic order of endpoint identifiers, with the direction-asserted field preserving which direction the source stated; the inverse edge is never stored as an independent assertion.
Time values canonicalise to RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset; an offset of -00:00 signals an unknown local offset and is preserved rather than rewritten to Z.
Confidence canonicalises to a decimal within the declared range together with its semantics code; an absent value stays absent and is never defaulted, rounded up, or replaced by a range midpoint.
The source-asserted predicate is stored verbatim alongside the local kind and is never normalised away.
patch_rules: Relation kind, subject identifier, object identifier and context-binding key are immutable; any change to them is performed by creating a superseding assertion linked to the original.

Strength and scope changes are recorded only through a supersession record carrying authority reference, change direction, reason and new effective interval; in-place edits of these fields are rejected.
Warrant fields may be corrected in place only with a recorded correction reason and retention of the prior value; a correction never changes the relation kind.
Adding a declared property to a relation-kind profile that was previously recorded as undeclared is a semantic change and requires a new kind identifier, not a patch.
Reports are never patched; a superseding report is produced against a new evaluated-set digest.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new relation kind or a new composition rule for a previously non-composable pair is additive and backward compatible, but must be versioned so consumers can detect it.
Changing the declared algebraic properties of an existing kind is breaking; the kind is deprecated and a new identifier is issued rather than the profile being rewritten.
Narrowing an existing composition rule is breaking for consumers that relied on the wider rule and requires a deprecation window; widening is additive but still versioned.

Alignment tables are versioned against the external specification version they were derived from; an external version change never silently rewrites stored assertions and instead raises a review obligation.
Consumers must treat an unknown relation kind as opaque and must not substitute the nearest known kind.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier assigned by the system of record that owns the artifact — for a relation-kind profile, the predicate IRI minted by the owning standards body; for an assertion, context binding, warrant or supersession record, the identifier assigned by the originating mapping system of record; for a report, the identifier assigned by the executing validation service.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in a resolvable, Dimension-controlled namespace when no master-system identifier exists, recorded together with the namespace authority.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as a last resort, explicitly marked as locally minted so consumers do not mistake it for an authoritative identifier.
A date, effective interval, source version, confidence value or evaluated-set digest is never an identifier and must not be used as, or embedded in, the key of any artifact.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; an offset of -00:00 means the local offset is unknown and is preserved as written. Event time and observation time are recorded separately and both retained whenever they differ: event time covers the instant the asserting agent made the claim and the effective interval over which the equivalence is claimed to hold, while observation or ingestion time covers the instant this model observed, received or ingested the assertion. Report generation time is a third, distinct instant and is never substituted for either.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — supersession records and conformance reports — are named as artifact-kind, then the identifier of the parent assertion or evaluated assertion set, then a zero-padded monotonic sequence number. Sequence numbers increase strictly per parent, are never reused after retraction, and carry no date-like or timestamp component; the generation time is a separate field.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored assertion carries a digest over its canonical form covering subject, predicate, object, context key and warrant references; changing any digested field requires a new assertion record rather than an update. Every conformance report records the digest of the assertion set and the constraint version it evaluated, so a report can be shown stale by comparison alone without re-running validation. Supersession records reference both the prior and superseding digests so a strength history can be verified without trusting narrative fields.

policies: Preserve asserted strength: never store or emit a relation kind stronger than the one the originating authority asserted. An incoming kind that cannot be expressed exactly is recorded as lossy with the original retained verbatim and a justification, never approximated upward.
Never fabricate certainty: a missing confidence is recorded as unknown, and no confidence value, however high, changes the relation kind or licenses an entailment the kind does not declare.

Closure and resolution are external: this model declares and validates semantics. It does not compute entailment or transitive closure, discover paths, resolve entities, follow or rewrite redirects, merge master data, or enforce any outcome.

Scope-unknown by default: an assertion without a declared context is not treated as globally valid, and a comparison between a declared scope and an unknown scope is reported as undetermined rather than compatible.

Report, do not repair: detected contradictions and exposure indicators are surfaced with severity and focus; disposition decisions and any corrective action belong to the named roles and to systems outside this model.

read: Read a relation-kind profile with its declared algebraic properties, applicability, cardinality force, owning specification version and deprecation state.
Read an alias assertion together with its context binding, warrant reference, state and supersession chain references.
Read declared composition rules and non-equivalence constraints for a given ordered kind pair or identifier pair.
Read the most recent conformance report reference and its evaluated-set digest without triggering re-validation.
create: Create a relation-kind profile only with a resolvable predicate IRI, an owning specification reference with version, and an explicit value — including undeclared — for symmetry, reflexivity, inverse pairing, composition, applicability and cardinality force.

Create an alias assertion only with exactly one catalogued kind, subject and object identifiers with referent types, a context binding or explicit scope-unknown marker, a justification type, an assertion instant and an observation instant.
Create a non-equivalence declaration only with the identifier pair or predicate set it denies, the declaring authority and its context binding.
Create a supersession record only through the authorised strength-change function, never as a bare insert.
update: Update is limited to non-semantic annotation such as comments, links to issue records and deprecation notes on a relation-kind profile.
Warrant fields may be corrected in place only with a recorded correction reason and retention of the prior value.
Semantic change to kind, subject, object, context key, strength or scope is performed by creating a superseding assertion; in-place mutation of these fields is rejected.
A relation-kind profile whose declared semantics change is deprecated and replaced by a new kind identifier rather than updated.
delete: Records of this model are not hard-deleted by default. A withdrawn assertion is tombstoned: its identifier, relation kind, context key, state of retracted and retraction authority are retained, while the warrant payload is dropped where the adopting Dimension's policy requires it, so that consumers holding the identifier can detect withdrawal rather than silently retaining a stale equivalence.

Retention periods and disposition classes for assertions, context bindings, warrant records, supersession records and conformance reports are set by the adopting Dimension's records-management policy. This model stores the retention-class reference on each record but does not compute or trigger expiry.

Execution of erasure, legal-hold handling, and preservation of the audit trail of deletions are owned by the adopting Dimension's records-management model and by the referenced audit model reached through the composition links. This model only marks a record as erasure-requested and stores the disposition outcome reported back to it; it neither performs erasure nor holds the audit trail.
Deleting or reusing a relation-kind profile identifier is prohibited while any assertion references it; the profile is marked deprecated and, where applicable, superseded by a new kind identifier.

Erasure of a warrant payload must not silently strengthen an assertion: where warrant is erased, the assertion's justification becomes unspecified and its confidence becomes unknown, and this transition is recorded.

roles.name: Relation-kind steward
responsibilities: Maintain the catalogue of relation kinds and their declared algebraic properties with clause-level citations.
Track owning specification versions and raise a review when an external body changes a predicate's semantics.
Deprecate kinds and issue new identifiers when declared semantics change, rather than rewriting a profile.

roles.name: Alias assertion curator
responsibilities: Create and curate assertions, ensuring exactly one catalogued kind, a valid context binding or explicit scope-unknown marker, and a recorded justification.
Record confidence only with its declared semantics and estimation method, and record unknown where no estimate exists.
Initiate supersession when an edge must be weakened, strengthened, rescoped or retracted.

roles.name: Context and jurisdiction owner
responsibilities: Define the Dimension's default context, jurisdiction and purpose code lists, and effective-interval conventions.
Rule on whether two declared scopes are incompatible when the comparison rules are ambiguous.
Approve any widening of an assertion's scope, since widening enlarges where substitution may be applied.

roles.name: Conflict reviewer
responsibilities: Review reported contradictions, invalid combinations and contagion exposure indicators and decide disposition.
Record the decision and the executing component without silently altering stored kinds or warrant.
Retain read access to retracted and deprecated assertions for dispute handling.

roles.name: Alignment liaison
responsibilities: Maintain alignment tables to external vocabularies against their published versions.
Record conflicts between external specifications and local practice without claiming conformance.
Ensure external version changes raise review obligations rather than silent rewrites of stored assertions.

access.default_rule: Relation-kind profiles, composition rules and non-equivalence declarations are readable by any agent authorised to read the host subject, because a consumer cannot safely interpret an edge without them. An individual alias assertion, its context binding and its warrant inherit the most restrictive access applying to either endpoint record, since an edge can disclose the existence of a restricted counterpart.
exceptions: Warrant fields that embed matching evidence, such as match strings or personal attributes used for linkage, are restricted to the alias assertion curator and conflict reviewer roles even where the assertion itself is broadly readable.

An assertion linking a pseudonymous identifier to a directly identifying identifier is treated as re-identifying and requires an explicit, time-bounded purpose grant that names the grantor and expiry.
Contagion exposure indicators may be released in aggregate form where the underlying edges are restricted, provided the aggregate cannot reconstruct a restricted edge.
Retracted, deprecated and superseded assertions remain readable to the conflict reviewer for dispute handling even after they are hidden from general consumers.
Where an edge is restricted but its relation kind is not, the kind profile remains readable so that a consumer encountering the edge elsewhere does not over-read it.
audit_requirements: Creation, supersession, retraction, tombstoning and purpose-grant decisions are emitted as events to the adopting Dimension's audit model; this model emits the event and does not store or own the audit trail.
Every conformance report records which assertion-set digest and which constraint or shape version it evaluated, so a later reader can determine whether the report still applies.
Re-identifying access grants record purpose, granting role, expiry and the assertion identifiers covered, and their retention is governed by the referenced records-management policy.
Any correction to a warrant field records the correction reason, the acting role and the prior value.

read_order: AGENTS.md — model name, type, registry identifier and the four resource URLs
Specification URL — model boundary, relation-kind catalogue, declared formal properties and context-scoping rules
Storage type URL — how assertions, context bindings, warrant, supersession records and reports project into the chosen store, whether document, graph, tabular or repository based
Interface URL — read, create, supersede and report-retrieval operations, including the explicit absence of any reasoning, traversal, resolution or merge operation
Processes URL — catalogue stewardship, assertion curation, supersession approval, conflict review and external alignment-update processes

coverage.claim: This structure covers the declared formal and contextual relation properties an agent needs in order to create, inspect and validate alias and same-as assertions without computing closure, resolving entities, following redirects or merging master data. Formal coverage is grounded in the OWL 2 axiom set and its direct semantics, the SKOS normative mapping statements S38 to S46, RDF 1.1 semantics on the absence of a unique name assumption, and RDF 1.2 statement annotation. Operational metadata coverage is grounded in the SSSOM mapping model, PROV-O attribution, SHACL report structure, DCMI succession terms, RFC 9110 relocation semantics and RFC 3339 timestamps, with schema.org v30.0 fixing the weakest published sense of sameAs.

checklist.notes: Identity priority names the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI in a controlled namespace, then a locally minted ULID marked as such. Endpoint referent types distinguish entity, concept, document and locator, and dates, intervals, source versions and digests are explicitly barred from being identifiers.

Assertion states cover active, expired, superseded, retracted and deprecated, with change performed only by supersession. Relation kinds are deprecated rather than rewritten when their semantics change. Execution of downstream propagation remains with consuming systems.

Symmetry, asymmetry, inverse pairing, reflexivity and irreflexivity are declared per kind with axiomatic force recorded, and composition rules are declared per ordered kind pair rather than assumed. Chain results are bounded by the weakest link.

Effective interval, assertion instant and observation instant are separate fields in RFC 3339 form with seconds and explicit offsets, and non-overlapping intervals are a named incompatibility code. Report generation time is a third distinct instant.

Asserting agent, activity or tool with version, generation time and justification type are recorded and reference the PROV-aligned provenance model without reproducing its lifecycle. The source-asserted predicate is retained verbatim.

The Dimension reference and binding owner are recorded per assertion; catalogue stewardship, assertion curation, context ownership, conflict review and alignment liaison are separately named roles with distinct authorities.

Declared-semantics checks cover applicability, cardinality force, disjointness, explicit non-equivalence and invalid combinations, reported with severity and focus pair against a recorded constraint version. Validation is reporting only; enforcement and remediation are external.

Assertions inherit the most restrictive endpoint access; matching evidence is role-restricted; re-identifying edges require a time-bounded purpose grant; four access scopes are declared. Enforcement points are outside the boundary.

Tombstoning with retained identifier, kind, context key and retraction authority is the default; retention-class references are stored but expiry is not computed here. Erasure execution, legal hold and audit preservation are owned by the Dimension's records-management and audit models, and warrant erasure is explicitly barred from silently strengthening an assertion.

Alignments to OWL 2 identity vocabulary, SKOS mapping properties, schema.org sameAs v30.0, SSSOM fields and DCMI succession terms are recorded as versioned alignments, with licensed and disclaimed entailments held per kind and no conformance claimed.

A declared partial order with incomparable pairs, a prohibition on promotion regardless of confidence, verbatim retention of the source-asserted predicate and a lossy-encoding flag together prevent silent strengthening on carriage.

Difference axioms, negated predicates and standard disjointness are first-class declarations, and exposure indicators quantify how many sources and classes a strength-of-identity edge would draw together before a consumer accepts it.
Jurisdiction and territorial scope are optional context attributes with an exclusivity flag and a named incompatibility code; code lists are supplied by the adopting Dimension rather than assumed.

Confidence carries a mandatory semantics declaration and estimation method, absence is recorded as unknown, and statistical linkage posteriors are explicitly distinguished from curator degrees of belief.

The model aligns to OWL 2, SKOS, SSSOM and schema.org but claims conformance to none of them. No published validation evidence for an OWL 2 profile or a SHACL shapes package was located during this research, so conformance would have to be demonstrated by the adopting Dimension before it is asserted.

known_omissions: The clause-level mapping typology of ISO 25964-2, covering exact, inexact, partial and compound equivalence, could not be verified from the standard text because the standard is paywalled; the catalogue therefore records no ISO 25964-2 alignment and a Dimension needing one must obtain the text and add it.

Behaviour of owl:sameAs applied to classes or properties under the RDF-based (OWL Full) semantics is flagged as a regime change but is not modelled in detail; only the OWL 2 DL applicability restriction is declared.

The choice between named-graph scoping and statement-level reifier annotation for context binding is deliberately left to the storage projection; RDF 1.2 is a Candidate Recommendation and its annotation mechanism may still change before Recommendation.
Label-based, multilingual and transliteration-sensitive matching heuristics are excluded, as matching is owned by the entity resolution model.
Bidirectional alignment to MADS and to ISO-style thesaurus data models is not covered, so vocabularies published only in those forms need an additional crosswalk.
No fixed numeric thresholds, score scales or default confidence values are supplied, because every cited source treats these as method- and domain-specific.
Cryptographic signing of assertions and of supersession records is not specified beyond the digest-based integrity rule.
conflicts: SKOS deliberately avoids owl:sameAs between concepts, because merging concepts would conflict with SKOS constraints on preferred labels, yet linked-data practice frequently asserts owl:sameAs between concept IRIs. The model records the asserted kind and reports the practice conflict rather than normalising either side.

schema.org documents sameAs as the URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity, with expected type URL and no declared entailment, whereas it is widely consumed as if it were owl:sameAs. Treating it as logical identity is a common but unsupported promotion.

SSSOM mapping cardinality values such as one-to-one are descriptive metadata about an observed mapping set, whereas FunctionalProperty, InverseFunctionalProperty and HasKey are axioms with real inferential force. Conflating the two is a recurring error, and HasKey additionally applies only to explicitly named individuals.

HTTP 301 and 308 permanently relocate a resource and permit clients to rewrite references, which concerns resolution of a locator and is not an assertion that two described things are identical. dcterms:isReplacedBy is likewise directional succession, not identity.

skos:exactMatch is declared transitive while skos:closeMatch is deliberately not, precisely so that similarity does not compound across schemes. Tools that chain match properties uniformly generate equivalences that no cited specification licenses.

OWL 2 DL restricts SameIndividual to individuals; asserting owl:sameAs between classes moves an ontology into OWL 2 Full and changes the available reasoning guarantees, so the same surface syntax carries different force depending on regime.

Probabilistic record linkage yields error-bounded statistical links whose quality depends on model assumptions and, in classical practice, on clerical review; a linkage posterior is a different quantity from a logical identity axiom and the two must not be stored under one predicate.
regional_assumptions: Jurisdiction codes and territorial scope values are supplied by the adopting Dimension; no particular national, supranational or industry code list is assumed or mandated.

Data-protection constraints on linking a pseudonymous identifier to a directly identifying identifier are assumed to exist in most jurisdictions, but their content varies and is referenced through a purpose grant rather than encoded in the model.
Language, script and transliteration of any labels used as matching evidence are recorded but no locale-specific normalisation is mandated, since normalisation rules differ by script and by domain.

Legal effect of a supersession or retraction, including whether a superseded equivalence must be actively unwound in downstream systems, is jurisdiction- and contract-specific and is left to the adopting Dimension.
Calendar and offset handling assumes RFC 3339 semantics only; no assumption is made about local civil-time rules, and -00:00 is preserved to signal an unknown local offset.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether a single symmetric and transitive alias predicate would suffice. Rejected: SKOS declares closeMatch symmetric but explicitly not transitive, and declares broadMatch and narrowMatch as an inverse pair, so a uniform algebra would over-generate equivalences that no source licenses.

Tested whether this model should own transitive closure so that consumers get a complete alias set. Rejected: closure and entailment are reasoner concerns referenced through a composition link. The model evaluates a declared composition rule over a caller-supplied edge sequence and never discovers paths or materialises inferences.

Tested whether a sufficiently high confidence value could promote closeMatch to exactMatch, or a linkage posterior to owl:sameAs. Rejected: no cited specification licenses strength promotion from a numeric score, and probabilistic linkage explicitly carries error rates and assumption dependence.

Tested whether dcterms:isReplacedBy or an HTTP 308 permanent redirect entails identity of the described thing. Rejected: both are directional relations about succession of a record or relocation of a resource, and RFC 9110 frames permanence as licence to rewrite references, not as an identity claim.

Tested whether the conformance report implies ownership of validation execution, enforcement or audit retention. Rejected: the report is a derived, non-authoritative structure aligned to an external validation model; execution, enforcement, persistence, retention and audit trail all sit with referenced models, and the delete rules name who owns erasure.

Tested whether schema.org sameAs could serve as the canonical predicate for the whole model, given its adoption. Rejected: its documented meaning is a reference web page indicating identity, its expected type is URL, and it declares no symmetry, transitivity, inverse or domain restriction beyond Thing.

Searched for a counterexample to uniform inverse pairing. Found one: broadMatch and narrowMatch are an OWL inverse axiom under SKOS S43, whereas dcterms:replaces and isReplacedBy are a documentary inverse pair without such an axiom. The model therefore records axiomatic force alongside every declared property instead of a bare boolean.

Tested whether an assertion with no declared context could be treated as globally valid to simplify consumption. Rejected: RDF's open-world reading means silence asserts nothing, and the identity literature documents referentially opaque contexts where substitution must not be applied, so scope-unknown is reported as undetermined rather than compatible.
